name: promote-agenttool-packages: widen the existing public repo into the development repo, and merge it back into private with real git merges
summary:
The public development repo would be the existing public cambridgetcg/agenttool-packages. It keeps its name, its 3-commit projection history, its rulesets and release tags, and the npm trusted-publisher binding, so nothing is re-pointed. It grows in stages:
- Stage 1: the 41 packages it already carries. This needs no content rulings: only 5 small rewrites sit inside the projected scope.
- Stage 1b: the other 21 packages.
- Stage 2: the public subset of api/, apps/, docs/ and bin/.

The private repo keeps its name and full history. Its tree is always the public tree plus private-only paths.

The core rule: **every path is either byte-identical in both trees or private-only.** All 524 rewrite and redact paths are cleaned once, in place in private. Then a guarded export copies those exact blobs onto the public head.

How the two repos connect:
- A one-time export E has the public head as its parent. A seed merge `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories E` in private then makes E the merge base. Every later merge-back is an ordinary 3-way merge, and it is clean whenever the rule above holds.
- I dry-ran this on the real trees in scratch:
  - E has 1,623 files.
  - The seed merge was clean and left the private tree unchanged.
  - Later public modifies, adds and deletes merged clean.
  - A widening export merged clean.
  - A private edit to a shared path was caught before the merge.

Runtime relational content moves into an optional `api/private/**` folder that only private builds include. The 40 checksum-frozen migrations move unchanged to `api/private/migrations/`; the 10 that contain DDL get idempotent public copies so fresh public installs build the same schema.

Leak defences:
- Private clones have no way to push to public (the push URL is disabled).
- Every public push and every public CI run requires the single public root commit 9b561523… and refuses a canary file planted in private. This was tested: pushed private history, an orphan branch and a copied private/ folder were all refused.
- A daily private scan with the relational word list covers public main and open PRs.

Deploy stays in private by default: private main is a merge of a public commit whose public CI already passed. Releases keep the npm trust as it is, with release tags that no longer require projection commits. PyPI gets a second trusted publisher.

Tree: exactly the shared paths of R, blob for blob; no PROJECTION.json. - Identity: fixed `AgentTool export `. Trailer: `Export-Source: `. - Built by `private/bin/public-export.ts`, a generalisation of project-public.ts. Once public CI (tree mode) is green, fast-forward main. This is allowed by "main is append-only", which blocks only deletion and non-fast-forward. 5. *Seed merge in private.* Run it on a branch cut at exactly R: - `git merge --no-ff --allow-unrelated-histories `. - Every path in E is an identical add on both sides, so merge-ort resolves cleanly and the merged tree equals R. Then merge that branch into private main normally. - From then on, `merge-base(private/main, public/main)` is E or later, so every later merge is a true 3-way merge. A replay must filter paths and mishandles both. - Public SHAs become ancestors of private main, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor ` proves inclusion. It switches to dev mode: a green ci.yml push run on main, and single-root history. The projection-history check is kept only up to de6778b1. - `npm-release.ts` accepts legacy projection tags (tagger `AgentTool projection`, Projection trailers) and new tags (tagger `AgentTool release`, trailers Package, Release-Commit and Public-CI-Run). - `RELEASE_REPOSITORY` and the CI-evidence code are unchanged. - 49 of 59 package.json repository.url fields name the private repo, and npm-release.ts:733 refuses them. yu_decisions: 1. Public development repo. Recommended: promote the existing public cambridgetcg/agenttool-packages and keep its name. This keeps the npm trust, free CI, rulesets and release tags with no re-pointing, and still meets 'open a public repo; develop there; merge back into private'. Alternative: a brand-new public repo. The same mechanics apply with E as its root commit, and agenttool-packages stays a release-only projection target (audit option a2).
2. Public main policy. Recommended: PR plus required checks (free on a public repo; a mistaken push then lands on a branch, not on append-only main). Alternative: agents push directly to main.

3. API and docs-site deploy. Recommended default: stay in private, deploying merged private main gated on the public CI run of the merged public parent. Stage 1 needs no change, secrets and deploy logs stay private, and prod needs no sealed-migration mode. Alternative: move deploy to public after stage 2, which needs SEALED.json in the runner and a production environment in agenttool-packages. Only needs deciding after stage 2.

4. Stage-2 content-ruling batch: audit decisions 5-10, 14 and 15 (persona wire enums, heart glyphs, two-name credits, quotes and anecdotes, already-live pages and the /public/law text, ops records, third-party content). Not needed for stage 1. Wire-enum allows are Ai-approvable under the denylist note.

5. Stage-1b licences: Apache-2.0 for gin-reconstruction, public-surface-binding and public-surface-recognition, wake-thread, collab-courier and correspondence-yutabase-projector; hold witnessed-agent-economy and karma-mirror private (audit decision 13).

Actions only Yu can do (not decisions): revoke the scope-wide NPM_TOKEN on npmjs.com and the old prod at_p_ key; add the second PyPI trusted publisher (agenttool-packages / publish-pypi.yml / pypi) in one 2FA session; approve the single epoch push to agenttool-packages.
risks: Private history leaks through an accidental push from one of the 12+ private checkouts. That history holds 9 old credentials and the relational corpus. Mitigations: a fetch-only pushurl; a private pre-push hook that refuses the public URL; a public pre-push hook and public CI that refuse any history whose root is not 9b561523a605…; a canary blob digest. Residual: GitHub accepts the objects before CI runs, so main should require PRs, and cleanup may need GitHub's sensitive-data removal.

Relational text written directly in a public PR is visible before the private scan runs. Mitigations: a pre-push relational scan on Yu's machines and a daily private scan of main and PR heads. The rest is accepted residual (audit decision 12).

Private edits to shared paths cause merge conflicts, or put private text at shared paths. Mitigations: a pre-commit refusal, the pre-merge drift check, and public wins on shared paths. A byte-identical upstream merges cleanly (verified).

add/add collisions with the roughly 200 legacy scattered keep-private paths when public later creates the same path. Mitigations: reserved namespaces for new private files, and a private PRIVATE-PATHS registry intersected before each merge, with lazy relocation into private/.

The release lane breaks at the epoch: public-release-tag.ts demands projection history, npm-release.ts demands the projection tagger and trailers, and public CI demands --history. Mitigation: dev-mode tags that still accept legacy tags, shipped in E, and a dry_run dispatch before any real stage.
Trust is coupled to the repo name. Renaming agenttool-packages later means re-pointing all npm and PyPI trust (inferred), so keep the name.
Public refactors break private overlay code (api/private/**) at merge time. Mitigation: private-scope gates on the merge branch, with fixes made only in private-only paths.
Generated indexes drift if private regenerates them. Mitigation: generators run in the public scope only, and the drift check catches anything else.
Shadow DDL migrations diverge from the 10 sealed DDL originals, so public CI tests a different schema from prod. Mitigation: a schema-dump equality test.
